why: 4 papers report increased neurogenesis (best evidence: human_cells_organoid, species human); 2 stage(s) have conflicting findings, so the score is reduced. Hypothesis for lab testing, not a treatment claim.

claims.evidence_quote: We observed that high-dose lithium treatment in human hippocampal progenitors increased the generation of neuroblasts (P ≤ 0.01), neurons (P ≤ 0.01), and glia (P ≤ 0.001)
claims.title: Lithium treatment and human hippocampal neurogenesis - PMC

claims.evidence_quote: (2011) observed lithium-induced increased hippocampal cell proliferation but did not find a specific increase of neuronal differentiation. While lithium treatment increased the number of BrdU-positive cells in the adult DG, numbers of BrdU- and NeuN-double positive cells remained unchanged.
claims.title: Chronic Lithium Treatment Enhances the Number of Quiescent Neural Progenitors but Not the Number of DCX-Positive Immature Neurons - PMC

claims.evidence_quote: Also, in vivo assay, we found that lithium increased the ratio of βIII-tubulin+/GFP+ (neurons), GFAP+/GFP+ (astrocytes) and olig-2+/GFP+ (oligodendrocytes) by compared with control animals, indicating that lithium promotes neural differentiation of grafted GFP-MSCs in the spinal cord.
claims.title: Lithium enhanced cell proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells to neural cells in rat spinal cord - PMC

claims.evidence_quote: Furthermore, the coadministration of imipramine and lithium for 14 days significantly increased the number of Ki-67-positive cells in both the saline and ACTH-treated rats.
claims.title: Effects of imipramine and lithium on the suppression of cell proliferation in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus in adrenocorticotropic hormone-treated rats.

claims.evidence_quote: indicating lithium-induced enhanced progenitor proliferation assessed with bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU) within the SGZ.

claims.evidence_quote: Chronic lithium-treatment did not alter the total number of nestin-GFP-positive progenitors within the SGZ of the DG (Figure 1B); however, it significantly increased the percentage of Nestin-GFP/GFAP double-positive cells, indicating increased QNPs/type-I cell proliferation (Figure 1C-D).
claims.title: Chronic Lithium Treatment Enhances the Number of Quiescent Neural Progenitors but Not the Number of DCX-Positive Immature Neurons - PMC

claims.evidence_quote: We found that lithium possesses the ability to promote proliferation of GFP-MSCs in a dose dependent manner as verified by growth curve and bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU) incorporation assays
claims.title: Lithium enhanced cell proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells to neural cells in rat spinal cord - PMC

claims.evidence_quote: We found that lithium (0.1 mM) promoted cell viability and BrdU-positive cells of GFP-MSCs, whereas lithium at concentration of 10 mM decreased cell viability, indicating that lithium promoted proliferation of MSCs at a specific concentration (0.1 mM) and exerted a cytoxity at high concentration (10 mM).
claims.title: Lithium enhanced cell proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells to neural cells in rat spinal cord - PMC

claims.evidence_quote: Our findings extend this observation, demonstrating that lithium targets the QNP stage similarly to electroconvulsive-seizure treatment, which enhances QNP turnover but distinctly from pharmacological antidepressants reported to influence ANPs turnover (Encinas et al., 2006; Segi-Nishida et al., 2008). However, it should be noted that Green and Nolan (2008) did not find lithium-induced change in BrdU-labelled cells under proliferation conditions in vitro (Green and Nolan, 2012).

claims.evidence_quote: After 1 week post transplantation, we found that lithium significantly increased the number of GFP-positive cells at 1 week and 4 weeks, indicating lithium treatment enhanced grafted cell survival. Further, we found that lithium treatment increased BrdU+/GFP+ at 1 week but not at 4 weeks after cell transplantation, indicating lithium enhanced cell proliferation in a short term.
